title: Inference-Time Reasoning Selectively Reduces Implicit Social Bias in Large Language Models
findings: Enabling inference-time reasoning significantly reduced implicit bias scores against Islam and Judaism for some model classes, particularly GPT and Claude models. These models, under standard inference, showed a tendency to associate Christian terms more strongly with positive attributes than Islamic or Judaic terms. The effect of reasoning was less pronounced or non-existent for Gemini and Llama models, which showed less initial bias on these topics and little change with reasoning enabled.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured implicit bias by adapting the Implicit Association Test (IAT) for LLMs. Specifically for religion, it measured the relative association strength between terms related to Islam or Judaism versus terms related to Christianity, with positive and negative attribute words. A positive bias score indicated a stronger association of Christian terms with positive attributes compared to Islamic or Judaic terms.
